title: Paper theatre
when: Editorial reveals, cultural essays and product moments built from apertures, folded planes and purposeful empty space
rules: Give the image a physical job: an opening reveals, a folded face redirects light, a sheet conceals then slips away.
Keep the copy left in landscape or in the top third of portrait. Let one large material object occupy the other area.
Use a didone for one short thought; keep evidence and body copy in clean native type outside the moving edges.
Cast shadows belong to objects. Avoid full-frame glow, orbiting ornaments and decorative particles.
Prefer a slow reveal followed by a held inspection. Use an iris only when the story moves through an opening.
